headline: Delegated review of the Complete Streets Prioritization Plan to a subgroup; elected Wathne chair and Guthrie vice chair.
summary: The committee discussed the Complete Streets Prioritization Plan and a draft response letter. Members voted to give the plan review to a subgroup, and several members expressed interest in meeting on July 13. The group also discussed a bikeshare station move, the July 4th Kids Bike Parade, and the Heritage Days Parade.
decisions: Approved delegating the committee's review of the Complete Streets Prioritization Plan to a subgroup, all in favor.
Approved changing the committee's meeting time to 6:15 p.m., all in favor.
Elected John Wathne as Chair, all in favor.
Elected Josiah Guthrie as Vice Chair, all in favor.
Approved the minutes of the 5/6/2026 and 6/3/2026 meetings, all in favor.
Agreed to resume the in-person/Zoom hybrid meeting format in August.

plain_text:
1 
 
Meeting Minutes 
 
Salem Bicycling & Shared Path Advisory Committee 
 
Wednesday, July 1, 2026 | 6:00 p.m. 
 
Via Remote Participation 
 
Members Present: John Wathne (Chair), Alexa Ogno, Craig Bilodeau, Matt Caruso, 
Kevin Jordan, Annie Wolf, Emmylou Manwill, Josiah Guthrie, Josh 
Nagle 
Members Absent:  Connor Ryan, Walter Morrell 
Also Present:  Tom Devine, Senior Planner 
 
 
Call Meeting to Order 
 
Guthrie presides in the Chair’s absence and calls the meeting to order at 6:21 p.m. 
Chair Wathne arrives at 6:41pm and presides 
 
Public Comment 
 
Guthrie opens the meeting to public comment and there is none. 
 
Discussion of Bike Master Plan 
 
Documents referenced: 
• Proposed Committee Logo (PNG graphic file) 
• W.I.P. 2026 Master Bike Plan Document, Discussion Starter: A Note on Terminology 
• Speculative Design Activity  
 
Guthrie shares a proposed logo and the group discusses possibilities. They request to 
continue the discussion at the next meeting. Guthrie also introduces the concept of 
emergent mobility and the group discusses. The group also discuss possibilities for 
improvements to the Washington and Bridge Street intersections, per Guthrie’s 
Speculative Design Activity. 
 
Complete Streets Prioritization Plan 
 
Documents presented: 
• Draft letter in response to Complete Streets Prioritization Plan 
• Complete Streets Prioritization Plan, Transportation Commission and Bicycle 
Advisory Committee Joint Meeting, 6/24/2026 
 
Devine explains that the city has a Complete Streets Prioritization Plan in order to be 
eligible for funding through the state’s complete street’s grant program and to inform
2 
 
selection of projects to consider funding with the program. The plan is periodically 
updated, as is happening now. The plan excludes projects that are being funded 
through other sources. These include some major projects like the reconstruction of 
Boston Street, Highland Ave., and Bridge Street. The plan was present at the June 24 
joint meeting with the Transportation Commission, though the Bike Committee did not 
achieve quorum and therefore participated as members of the public. Members of the 
two bodies agreed that the Bike Committee should continues it review at tonight’s 
meeting. 
 
Guthrie shared a draft writeup stating that the plan doesn’t represent the group’s values 
in the most effective way. Wathne noted the approach is intense. Ogno stated that the 
group needs to move the needle and be more proactive in its advocacy. Manwill 
questioned whether the community is ready. Devine suggested that strong criticism is 
welcome in public dialog, but it is most effective when given in the context of strong 
partnerships and relationships in the community. Wathne shared thoughts about being 
led by both reality and idealism. Manwill suggested noting criticism but then highlighting 
the positives in the plan that we want to see more of. Nagle proposed showing 
examples of what they want to see and note the committee’s values. 
 
Guthrie remarks that while he may always be a radical voice, he also wants to be part of 
a consensus. He explains that the group isn’t required to have technical expertise and 
values are the core thing they can represent. Caruso says he thinks the approach 
should be more balanced and constructive. Nagle says they should have a thoughtful 
tone, but still ask for as much as possible, considering the City Council is supportive of 
our work. Bilodeau suggests softening the tone and including specific feedback, such as 
his concern about how bikes will be accommodated at the planned Jefferson Ave. and 
Jackson Street roundabout. Manwill laments that nothing new has been pedestrianized 
since the pedestrian mall was in the 1970s. Wathne suggests a subgroup to review the 
plan more specifically. 
 
Guthrie, Ogno, Jordan, and Wathne express interest in meeting on July 13 to review 
further. Bilodeau and Caruso are also interested but not available. 
 
Guthrie motions, Nagle seconds, and all vote in favor to delegate the Committee’s 
review of the Complete Streets Prioritization Plan to the subgroup. 
 
Bikeshare Program Updates 
 
Devine reports that, due to construction, the Salem State North Campus station is 
moving from the Alumni Plaza at the Ellison Campus Center to Lafayette Street in front 
of Meier Hall. This is a permanent move and Devine believes it is a location that will 
serve not just the campus, but the neighborhood too, as it will be more visible outside 
the campus. 
 
July 4th Kids Bike Parade
3 
 
The group discusses logistics of the event at Salem Common. It begins with bike 
decorating at 11am and police on bikes leading the parade around the path inside the 
Common. O’Donnell’s Funeral Home will provide popsicles afterwards in their rear 
parking lot and Ogno will set up a bike rodeo course. Devine will confirm proper 
channels for communicating to the public in the event of cancellation due to weather. 
 
8/1/2026 Heritage Days Parade 
 
Devine states that the deadline passed to register and no one expressed strong interest 
in the Committee participating. Devine suggests that if any individuals want to 
participate, they should join another group that is registered. 
 
Group Rides 
 
Ogno says she would like to see more Bike Committee members at group rides and 
suggests everyone should get on Christine Madore’s bike email list. Ogno is planning 
an August or September taco ride and maybe a chocolate ride too. 
 
Other Events 
 
The group discusses their experience marching in the North Shore Pride Parade. 
 
Transportation Commission Update 
 
Manwill notes that the last meeting was the June 24 joint meeting with this Committee. 
 
Staff Update 
 
Ogno says she attended a listening session about the 2026 Strategic Highway Safety 
Plan. She says it is focused on roads in general and there is an interactive tool to gather 
public input. She also says that she is surprised at Salem’s low People for Bikes 
Ranking, with Middleton scoring highest in the state. 
 
Devine announces that there is now sufficient building staff to resume meeting in-
person and the group agrees to resume their in-person/Zoom hybrid format in August. 
 
Devine reports that the Fort Lee preservation plan is underway and notes that biking is 
found to cause damage to the historic asset. He suggests this is an opportunity for the 
committee to have a better relationship with preservation advocates. 
 
Devine announces that Walter Morrell has resigned from the committee due to some 
new obligations in his life, but he hopes to continues to see everyone and find 
opportunities to remain involved. The group discusses outreach to recruit a new 
member.
4 
 
Guthrie motions, Caruso seconds, and all vote in favor to change their meeting time to 
6:15pm. 
 
Election of Chair and Vice Chair 
 
Bilodeau nominates Wathne as Chair, Manwill seconds, and all vote in favor. 
 
Wolf nominates Guthrie to be Vice Chair, Ogno seconds, and all vote in favor. 
 
Meeting Minutes 
 
Nagle motions, Caruso seconds, and all vote in favor to approve the 5/6/2026 and 
6/3/2026 minutes. 
 
Adjourn 
 
Caruso motions, Nagle seconds, and all vote in favor to adjourn at 8:09pm. 
 
*** 
 
Approved by the Bicycling & Shared Path Advisory Committee on 8/5/2026.
